I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation that people here know well, because in Quzhou County that is the steadiest way for me to use the land, water, and labor. I am 65, so I will not spread myself across too many crops. I want work that is familiar, easy to arrange, and less risky. I will plant winter wheat on all my land, then after harvest I will plant summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care more about stable yield than saving seed. I will not use very heavy fertilizer, because that costs money and can lodge the crop, but I will still feed the land enough to protect yield. Water is always important here, so I will irrigate wheat more than maize, and I will watch the weather and soil moisture. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage and fits common machinery use. I will spray only as needed, mainly for weeds, aphids, armyworm, and common diseases, because I want to control problems without wasting cash.
